content.text: , an immersive exhibition presented by W.A.S.+

W.A.S (Whaffle, Andre, and Sola) is a collective dedicated to preserving Black history and culture through art, photography, design, installation, and archival practice. W.A.S+ expands that mission through collaborations with artists, collectors, and cultural partners.

explores Black interior design, media, culture, and memory through the recreation of a 1960s–1970s basement. More than a nostalgic recreation, the installation examines how Black homes became spaces of identity, creativity, connection, and community. It also reflects on the importance of preserving these environments, along with the stories, objects, and memories they hold.
The exhibition features a selection of archival objects from the collection of StorageBased, further deepening the historical narratives that underpin the exhibition.

Whether you're just getting started with AI coding agents (beginner friendly!) or you've been shipping with them for months, you'll walk away with practical techniques you can use the next day.

Huge thanks to our sponsors, MongoDB and Clickhouse!

for Atlas credits and Voyage AI tokens, technical expertise, and dedicated support on the world’s best modern, AI-ready data platform.

Each presentation will be ~10 minutes with a ~5 minute Q&A, 7 presentations total. We don't expect to use the full 2.5 hours for presentations, but we're estimating conservatively.

is the head of product engineering and first engineering hire at Warp. He's been building agents for 5 years at Warp, helping scale it to millions of active users. is the CEO of Nori, the lead organizer of Agentics, and the author of

. He's been in the AI world for 12 years, including a 4-year stint at Google Research. Nori uses background agents to do just about everything — an army of agents respond to errors, manage the CRM, keep data clean, and more. In his talk, Amol will walk through what a "software factory" is, how to build one, and what pitfalls to avoid.

is the founder and core maintainer of LibreChat. He was early to recognize the need for cross-provider dev tools, and started LibreChat 3 years ago to create a chat UI experience separated from the big labs. Danny will be speaking about how LibreChat solved multiplayer agent/human sandboxes.

is a software engineer on the Goose team at Block and one of the most prolific contributors to Goose, Block's open-source AI agent. His Goose work spans the multi-provider LLM architecture, MCP integration, and the Goose SDK. Jack will speak about unbundling the Goose harness into an SDK and the uses that emerge from treating agents as SDKs.

is a two-time founder and ex-Googler, and the current CEO of subconscious.dev. LLMs are incredible tools with one massive limitation: the context window. They are fundamentally limited in what they can remember. Jack has spent the last two years thinking about how to make this problem better. He'll be speaking about context compression and long-horizon tasks in modern LLMs.

is the CTO and cofounder of Opus. Over the last 6 years, Jeff has spent a lot of time thinking about how to build tools that benefit everyone at Opus, including non-technical team members. is an early Member of Technical Staff at Modal and a Penn M&T grad. Joy will show you how to vibe train a model on Modal Training Gym, an RL library that lets users post-train on Modal in under 100 lines of code.

This effort is founded on the belief that soft-surface trails provide a public health benefit for New Yorkers by increasing accessibility to the outdoors and replacing recreational activity on hard surfaces that can increase bodily injuries. Beginning with sharing education about existing trails, the long-term goal of the project is to improve maintenance of and increase investment in New York City’s trails.

content.text: Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI.

We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly and effortlessly — the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, and the same songs, restaurants, and aesthetics rise to the top everywhere.

What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict and automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human — our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives — turned into data, and data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, and it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.
The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets and the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are.

Camille is the Senior Director of Strategy and Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed and developed in the public interest. content.text: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7. Drinks included in ticket.

Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN and CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there.
So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch?

For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders.

For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, and worse actors. Polymarket and Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had.
One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market.
Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology and the author of
How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It)

She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, and contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, and Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households and classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies.
Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, and has run client engagement at Norm AI

, anthe AI company building legal and compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF and a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, and roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant.
Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have.
Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, and Democracy Now!,

with features in Vanity Fair and New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days and elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race and calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided.
Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

content.text: Join Counterspell Games at Love & Legends Books, as we get crafty with a selection of fantasy themed activities!
Spend the evening off your screen and step into a magical fantasy world. From painting minis, to paper crafts, to pinnable buttons, this is your chance for creativity!

"Mini painting" (short for miniature painting) is the hobby of hand-painting small figurines used in tabletop roleplaying games (TTRPGs) to help visualize a character's movement. Our minis are pre-primed and ready to paint! We'll show you the techniques you need to make a new character, or bring your existing one to life.
Use our button maker and select your favorite fantasy imagery to create your own pinnable buttons! Wear them on your jacket, pin to your backpack, or give them to a friend.
🗡️ NEW: Make an enchanted crown and sword

Along your adventures you might find magical objects, but have you ever tried crafting one before? We'll show you how to make a beautiful sword and crown out of just paper, glue, and plenty of bedazzlement! What will you name your sword? At which jaunty angle will you wear your crown? Only you can decide!
Your ticket includes one mini, one fantasy crown, one fantasy sword, and three buttons!
We'll also provide you with a protective sleeve for your paper crafts, and a container to take your painted mini safely home with you :)
Never rolled a D20 before? No worries!
This is a great opportunity to explore the world of tabletop games for a spell. And if you regularly play TTRPGs like D&D or Daggerheart, we hope the evening inspires you for your next adventure.
❤️ “It was so fun!!! More things that involve imagination + art/creation :)“
🤩 “The time flew by, I was in the zone"
🎨 “I loved being able to make a new character.”
Everything you need to get creative.
We provide all the crafting materials, from paint to paintbrushes, paper and glue, and a selection of heroic miniatures to choose from.
Counterspell Games events are completely in person, with no screens. Take a break from notifications and doomscrolling, meet new people, and share in a truly analog experience.
Check out Love & Legends' offerings as you craft!
Stock up on your favorite fantasy series, pick up some new dice, or check out their curated selection of TTRPGs.
